meaning: The number of men from Kiriath-jearim, Kephirah and Beeroth who returned from the Babylonian exile
description: The number 743 appears in the biblical censuses after the return from Babylon. In both Ezra 2:25 and Nehemiah 7:29, this is given as the number of descendants or men from the three cities Kiriath-Jearim, Gibeon, and Beeroth. These three cities belonged to the territory of the tribe of Benjamin and were among the places that were repopulated after the exile. The number testifies to the scale of the return and to the painstaking rebuilding of the Jewish community in the land after the Babylonian captivity. Beyond this concrete historical context, the number 743 has no well-established symbolic meaning in classical biblical numerology or Jewish tradition.

versions.meaning: The number 743 has no well-established or known symbolic meaning in biblical or Jewish tradition.
versions.description: In biblical numerology and Jewish gematria, it is primarily simple numbers, as well as certain composite numbers with specific links to Hebrew words, that are attributed symbolic significance. The number 743 does not appear as a prominent number in the Bible or in classical Jewish texts with an acknowledged symbolic role. Through gematria, the number can potentially be linked to Hebrew words or phrases that sum to 743, but this does not constitute a widely accepted or traditional symbolic meaning.
versions.reason: [major] The number 743 appears explicitly in Ezra 2:25 and Nehemiah 7:29 as the count of descendants/men from Kiriath-Jearim (Kiriath-Arim), Gibeon, and Beeroth. This is a concrete biblical occurrence that should be mentioned in the description. To say that the number 'does not appear as a prominent number in the Bible' is directly incorrect when it is actually mentioned in two verses.; [major] The meaning field states that the number has no known symbolic significance, but it does have a concrete biblical context as the number of returnees from three cities after the exile. Although it lacks deep symbolic meaning, this biblical context should be noted.; [minor] The biblical context of the return from Babylon to three specific towns in the tribe of Benjamin is historically interesting and deserves a footnote about its historical background.

footnotes.text: Kiriath-jearim is known from 1 Samuel 7:1–2 as the place where the ark of the covenant was kept for twenty years after it was returned by the Philistines. The name means 'city of forests'.

Kephirah and Beeroth are mentioned in Joshua 9:17 as Gibeonite cities that made a treaty with Israel through deception. That descendants from these cities returned from exile shows that they had become fully integrated into Israel's community.
The difference in the name form Kiriath-arim (Ezra 2:25) and Kiriath-jearim (Nehemiah 7:29) represents a common shortened form of the city name in Hebrew. Both refer to the same city.
